title: Advanced Observability with Amazon CloudWatch (CloudWatch Advanced Workshop)
content:
This hands-on lab on Advanced Observability with Amazon CloudWatch (CloudWatch Advanced Workshop) was conducted on Monday (26/10/2026) as part of Week 7. This document provides an exhaustive operational walkthrough covering automated infrastructure deployment via AWS CloudFormation, advanced metric calculations (Metric Math, Search Expressions, Dynamic Labels), log stream diagnostics using CloudWatch Logs Insights, log metric filters, multi-channel alerting with Amazon SNS, and operational dashboard creation.
🎯 Lab Objectives: Automate the provisioning of a multi-instance compute fleet (Instance-A through Instance-E) using an AWS CloudFormation template (AwsWorkshopStack). Master dynamic metric queries using Metric Math and automated Search Expressions (SEARCH('used', 'Average', 300) and SEARCH('disk_used_percent', 'Average')), allowing monitoring graphs to dynamically accommodate new instances without manual dashboard reconfiguration. Standardize telemetry graph legends using Dynamic Labels ${PROP('Dim.DimName')} and ${PROP('Dim.InstanceId')} to enhance visual clarity and operational identification. Connect securely to EC2 instances without opening inbound port 22 using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager (SSM), and execute a synthetic telemetry script (logger.py) pushing multi-level events to /var/log/messages. Harness the full analytical capabilities of CloudWatch Logs Insights: write regex error filtering queries (like /ERROR/, like /WARN/), compute stream distribution aggregations (stats count(*) by @logStream), and render time-bucketed event histograms (stats count(*) by bin(5m)). Extract quantifiable telemetry from unstructured log files using CloudWatch Metric Filters (PythonAppErrors), configure CloudWatch Alarms (PythonApplicationErrorAlarm1) integrated with Amazon SNS email notifications, and construct a centralized operations dashboard ssmDashboard. 📊 Summary of Deployed Infrastructure & Parameters: Component / Resource Logical Name / Identifier Technical Specifications Region / AZ Operational Purpose CloudFormation Stack AwsWorkshopStack Status: CREATE_COMPLETE, provisions lab infrastructure us-east-1 Automated deployment of compute, networking, and IAM EC2 Test Instance A ssmStack/Instance-A/test-instance (i-01438dfe66b5e77ce) Type: t4g.micro, Arch: Graviton (arm64), Zone: us-east-1a us-east-1a Host generating simulated log data and error telemetry EC2 Cluster (B-E) InstanceBtestinstance … InstanceEtestinstance Multi-instance target cluster for metric expressions us-east-1 Compute cluster monitored via dynamic metric searches SSM /ec2/linux/var/log/messages Stream ID: i-0e4862b2e5b03d06a / i-01438dfe66b5e77ce us-east-1 Ingests operating system and application log events Metric Filter PythonAppErrors Pattern: [..., appId="logger.runJob:", message="ERROR*"] Log Group Transforms unstructured ERROR log lines into numeric metrics SNS Alarm Topic Default_CloudWatch_Alarms_Topic ARN: arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:887086382708:... us-east-1 Delivers instant email notifications upon alarm state change CloudWatch Alarm PythonApplicationErrorAlarm1 Threshold: ERROR > 10 for 1 datapoints within 5 mins Metric Filter Flags application degradation when error rate crosses threshold Custom Dashboard ssmDashboard-1dDcqviqU6D2 Widgets: Commands, Success/Fail sums, Error Alarm us-east-1 Unified single-pane-of-glass executive observability console 🚀 Step-by-Step Implementation & Screenshot Evidence: Part 1: Automated Infrastructure Provisioning with CloudFormation Step 1: Deploy CloudFormation Stack AwsWorkshopStack Action: Sign in to the AWS Console in us-east-1 (N. Virginia) ➔ Open AWS CloudFormation ➔ Click Create stack ➔ Upload the workshop infrastructure template. Execution: Monitor the creation lifecycle of dependent resources (VPC, subnets, instance profiles, and EC2 instances A through E). The stack successfully reaches CREATE_COMPLETE status with all instances provisioned. Part 2: Dynamic Metric Math, Search Expressions & Dynamic Labels Step 2: Implement Dynamic Metric Discovery with Search Expressions Action: Open Amazon CloudWatch ➔ Navigate to Metrics ➔ Select Classic metrics ➔ Open the Graphed metrics tab ➔ Click Add math ➔ Search expression. Query Definitions: Expression 1: SEARCH("disk_used_percent", 'Average', 300) Expression 2: SEARCH('used', 'Average', 300) Operational Value: As new instances are launched into the autoscaling fleet, CloudWatch automatically evaluates the expression and graphs their telemetry without manual updates. Step 3: Metric Math Multi-Variable Calculation Action: Apply Metric Math formulas to compute aggregate utilization percentages across multiple metrics dynamically. Step 4: Legend Standardization with Dynamic Labels Action: In the Label column of the search expression, configure dynamic parameter extraction: ${PROP('Dim.DimName')} or extract specific instance identifiers using ${PROP('Dim.InstanceId')}. Result: Replaces confusing raw metric strings with clean, human-readable labels indicating the exact target instance name. Part 3: Remote Administration via Systems Manager & Telemetry Simulation Step 5: Verify EC2 Instance-A Health Action: Navigate to Amazon EC2 ➔ Search by tag test-instance ➔ Select ssmStack/Instance-A/test-instance (i-01438dfe66b5e77ce). Specifications: The workload runs on Graviton-powered ARM64 architecture (t4g.micro), reporting 3/3 checks passed. Step 6: Establish Secure Terminal Session via SSM Session Manager Action: Click Connect ➔ Select Session Manager ➔ Click Connect to open a secure browser shell without requiring SSH key pairs. Deploy Synthetic Logger: cd /tmp nano logger.py sudo chmod +x logger.py python3 logger.py & ps -aux | grep logger The script emits synthetic INFO, WARN, and ERROR logs to /var/log/messages. Step 7: Inspect Real-Time Log Emission Action: Tail the live system log stream: sudo tail -f /var/log/messages Output: Periodic logs formatted with logger.py: AWS-Workshop-Test: This is a dummy ERROR message for CloudWatch Logs Insights lab stream continuously to the CloudWatch Agent. Part 4: High-Performance Log Analytics with CloudWatch Logs Insights Step 8: Inspect Ingested Log Groups & Streams Action: Navigate to CloudWatch ➔ Logs ➔ Log management ➔ Select log group /ec2/linux/var/log/messages. Execution: Select log stream i-0e4862b2e5b03d06a and confirm that operating system telemetry is successfully ingested into CloudWatch. Step 9: Execute Baseline Logs Insights Query Action: In the left menu, click Logs Insights ➔ Select /ec2/linux/var/log/messages ➔ Set time range to 1 hour (1h). Query Statement: fields @timestamp, @message | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20 Click Run query to inspect the 20 most recent log entries. Step 10: Advanced Regex Pattern Filtering for ERROR and WARN Events Filter for ERROR logs: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /ERROR/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20 Filter for WARN logs: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /WARN/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20 Step 11: Statistical Grouping & Time-Series Visualization Group error counts by Log Stream: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /ERROR/ | sort @timestamp desc | stats count(*) by @logStream Time-bucketed aggregation rendered as Line chart: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /eth0/ | sort @timestamp desc | stats count(*) by bin(5m) Step 12: Save Query Definition for Operational Runbooks Action: Click Save ➔ Name the query cloudwatch-workshop/ERROR to allow on-call engineers to run diagnostics instantly during incidents. Part 5: Log Metric Filters, SNS Alerts & Centralized Dashboard Step 13: Create Log Metric Filter Action: In /ec2/linux/var/log/messages, select Metric filters ➔ Click Create metric filter. Filter Specification: Filter Pattern: [month, day, timestamp, host, appId="logger.runJob:", message="ERROR*"] Validate pattern matching via Test pattern. Name the filter PythonAppErrors, set Metric Namespace to CustomAppMetrics, and Metric Value to 1. Step 14: Confirm Amazon SNS Subscription Action: In Amazon SNS, create topic Default_CloudWatch_Alarms_Topic and subscribe the engineer’s email address. Verification: Confirm subscription via the validation email. The browser confirms Subscription confirmed!. Step 15: Create CloudWatch Alarm & Finalize ssmDashboard Action: Create alarm PythonApplicationErrorAlarm1 monitoring PythonAppErrors where ERROR > 10 for 1 datapoints within 5 mins. Route notification actions to the SNS Topic. Unified Operations Dashboard: Navigate to Dashboards ➔ Build ssmDashboard-1dDcqviqU6D2 integrating Systems Manager command execution widgets alongside live health status indicators for PythonApplicationErrorAlarm1. 💡 Lessons Learned & Troubleshooting Bank: Below are 5 practical operational takeaways and troubleshooting strategies from advanced CloudWatch implementations:
1. Metric Math vs Automated Search Expressions Challenge: Traditional Metric Math queries require explicit instance IDs. Dynamic Auto Scaling environments fail to capture newly launched compute nodes. Solution: Leverage SEARCH() expressions with tag filters or namespace constraints to dynamically discover and chart metrics as workloads scale. 2. Strict Space-Delimited Syntax in Metric Filter Patterns Caution: Space-delimited filter patterns [field1, field2, field3...] require exact positional alignment with log tokens. For structured logs, prioritize JSON filter syntax { $.level = "ERROR" }. 3. Zero-Trust Access via AWS Systems Manager Session Manager Security Architecture: Disabling inbound port 22 and enforcing SSM Session Manager eliminates bastion host maintenance, enforces IAM role-based session authorization, and logs complete session transcripts to S3/CloudWatch. 4. Query Cost Optimization in CloudWatch Logs Insights FinOps Governance: Logs Insights charges per gigabyte of ingested data scanned. Restricting query windows to narrow time horizons (1h, 3h) substantially mitigates query costs. 5. Safe Resource Decommissioning Lifecycle Clean-Up Procedure: Delete CloudFormation stack AwsWorkshopStack to tear down instances, VPCs, and IAM roles. Delete alarm PythonApplicationErrorAlarm1 and SNS topic Default_CloudWatch_Alarms_Topic. Delete dashboard ssmDashboard-1dDcqviqU6D2 and retention policies on /ec2/linux/var/log/messages.

title: Introducing AWS Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
content:
Link to Author’s Published Community Post: View post on Facebook AWS Study Group - First Cloud Journey Original Article Reference: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available (AWS News Blog — Author: Esra Kayabali, GA: October 22, 2026). 1. Background & The DevSecOps Triage Bottleneck In modern cloud-native development, AI-assisted coding tools have dramatically accelerated development velocity. However, this velocity also causes the volume of reported security vulnerabilities to scale exponentially.
Traditional static application security testing (SAST) and software composition analysis (SCA) tools typically generate thousands of raw findings daily, triggering severe operational fatigue. Conventional scanners inspect source code in isolation without understanding cloud infrastructure topology. As a result, a Critical severity finding on an internal offline developer utility receives the same alarm priority as a Medium flaw exposed on a public checkout API sitting directly in front of a payments database. Security teams expend days coordinating across application and infrastructure engineers just to answer a basic question: is this vulnerability truly reachable and exploitable in our live production environment? Crafting and shipping code patches often stalls because engineering teams lack the business context to safely evaluate the blast radius of proposed changes.
To resolve these chronic challenges, on October 22, 2026, AWS announced the General Availability (GA) of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities — an autonomous security service powered by frontier AI models that validates exploitable flaws and delivers remediations directly as reviewed pull requests in your repositories.
2. Architectural Breakthrough: How AWS Continuum Operates Unlike traditional alerting scanners, AWS Continuum establishes a closed-loop, automated remediation lifecycle connecting repository source code with live AWS infrastructure topology:
Continuum’s operational model is built on four core technological pillars:
Bidirectional Context Graph: Continuum correlates signals across repository source code and live AWS environments via the AWS Continuum Collector agent. The collector extracts telemetry from AWS Config, VPC routing, security groups, and IAM policies to determine whether vulnerable components are exposed to untrusted networks or handle sensitive data, prioritizing alerts based on actual business risk. Isolated Exploit Validation: For plausible vulnerabilities, Continuum spins up isolated managed sandboxes to execute reproducible proof-of-concept exploits. Findings receive explicit validation tiers (Static proven, Exploit verified), along with full attack path documentation and blast radius assessments. Automated Remediation Pull Requests: Once an exploit is verified, the AI Remediation Engine synthesizes a high-fidelity code fix (patching source logic, upgrading dependencies, or correcting resource policies). Continuum automatically opens a Pull Request named Continuum fix directly on GitHub/GitLab, complete with risk explanations and test evidence. Human-in-the-Loop Governance: Continuum never mutates source code or modifies production infrastructure autonomously. Every remediation is delivered as a standard pull request for engineer and tech lead review and approval prior to merging. 3. Hands-On Tour: AWS Console & GitHub Integration Within the AWS Management Console, the Continuum Overview dashboard provides centralized visibility across connected repositories, runtime environments, and collector health:
Instead of unprioritized alert backlogs, Continuum displays only issues proven to be exploitable, organized by operational severity and remediation readiness:
Each finding features a comprehensive risk report detailing validation proof (Static proven), reachability (Exploitable), potential tenant impact, and the exact lines of offending source code:
Most importantly, Continuum generates production-grade Pull Requests on GitHub with precise diffs and clear change rationales, enabling engineers to inspect, test, and merge remedies efficiently:
4. Key Takeaways for Cloud Engineers & DevSecOps Teams The release of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities represents a pivotal transition in cloud security:
From Passive Detection to Autonomous Remediation: Rather than merely routing defect tickets to developers, Continuum actively participates in the development lifecycle by authoring validated, production-ready code patches. Eliminating Dev-Sec Friction: Security teams receive verifiable proof of exploitability, while developers save hours of manual triage, sustaining feature velocity without compromising posture. Controlled Frontier AI Adoption: Continuum demonstrates how agentic AI can automate complex security engineering tasks while maintaining strict human approval boundaries.

title: Resource Limit Governance with AWS Service Quotas
content:
The Resource Limit Governance with AWS Service Quotas lab was completed on Monday (19/10/2026) as part of Week 6. This page provides comprehensive documentation of reviewing default service quotas, initiating an account-level quota increase request for EC2 Spot Instances (All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests, Quota code L-34B43A08) from 32 to 64 vCPUs in the us-east-1 region, analyzing cloud cost implications, tracking the resolution lifecycle via AWS Support Center (Case ID: 179257232100832), receiving formal confirmation emails from Amazon Web Services, and automating quota queries with the AWS CLI.
🎯 Lab Objectives: Understand the core concept and strategic role of AWS Service Quotas in enterprise cloud governance, billing safeguard enforcement, and account infrastructure defense. Distinguish between Soft Limits (service limits that can be increased via request) and Hard Limits (immutable physical or architectural boundaries enforced by AWS). Master the modern Amazon EC2 quota paradigm: understanding how AWS calculates computing thresholds based on cumulative vCPUs rather than raw server instance counts. Execute a formal Request Quota Increase workflow, scaling compute capacity from 32 to 64 vCPUs for standard EC2 Spot Instances (All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests). Experience interactive client-side Input Validation on the AWS Management Console when attempting to enter invalid quota thresholds. Learn the inter-service communication workflow between customer accounts and the AWS Support Center under the Basic Support Plan. Resolve a fundamental cloud economics (Cloud FinOps) dilemma: Does requesting or getting approved for a Service Quota increase incur any financial charges? Leverage the AWS CLI (aws service-quotas) to automate quota discovery, query specific limits, inspect historical change requests, and script compliance validation. Establish Proactive Quota Monitoring by designing CloudWatch Alarms that notify operators when resource consumption approaches 80% and 95% of the allocated ceiling. 📊 Provisioned Resource Specifications: Parameter / Resource Actual Value Technical Significance & Role AWS Service Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) Core compute service providing scalable virtual computing capacity in the cloud Quota Name All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests Cumulative vCPU threshold for standard compute-family Spot Instances Quota Code L-34B43A08 Canonical AWS identifier for standard Spot vCPU allocation Target Region us-east-1 (US East - N. Virginia) AWS geographic region where the quota applies Default Quota Value 32 vCPUs Out-of-the-box ceiling configured by AWS for the account Requested Quota Value 64 vCPUs New requested compute ceiling submitted for AWS approval Support Case ID 179257232100832 Automated case tracking identifier created in AWS Support Center Account Support Plan Basic Support Standard non-paid support tier included with all AWS accounts Resolution Status Case Closed / Approved Request successfully validated and granted by AWS technical engineers Propagation Time Within 30 minutes Time required to synchronize the new quota across global distributed fleets Notification Channel Official email from Amazon Web Services Administrator inbox receiving official approval verification 📋 Detailed Step-by-Step Implementation Guide: 🔹 Module 1: Exploring AWS Service Quotas & Inspecting EC2 Limits Step 1: Navigate to the AWS Service Quotas Console Action: Sign in to the AWS Management Console ➔ Type Service Quotas into the top search bar ➔ Select Service Quotas from the services list. Verify Region: Confirm in the top navigation bar that the active region is US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1. Note that the vast majority of AWS infrastructure quotas are enforced independently per geographic region (Per-Region Quotas). Objective: The Service Quotas dashboard provides a centralized pane of glass to view default values, current applied values, and utilization percentages across over 250 AWS services. Step 2: Navigate to Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) Action: On the left navigation pane, click AWS services ➔ In the service filter search box, enter EC2 or Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) ➔ Click the service name to inspect its catalog of configurable quotas. Observation: EC2 manages hundreds of distinct quotas covering Elastic IPs, VPC Peering limits, Launch Templates, and vCPU quotas categorized by instance families (Standard, High Memory, Accelerated Computing) and pricing models (On-Demand vs Spot). Step 3: Filter for the Standard Spot vCPU Quota Action: In the quota search box (Filter quotas), enter: All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests. Displayed Metadata: Quota name: All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests Quota code: L-34B43A08 Default value: 32 (vCPUs) Applied value: 32 (vCPUs) Significance: This quota dictates that within us-east-1, the account can run concurrent standard Spot instances up to a collective sum of 32 vCPUs. For example, 16 instances of t3.medium (2 vCPUs x 16 = 32 vCPUs) or 4 instances of c5.2xlarge (8 vCPUs x 4 = 32 vCPUs). 🔹 Module 2: Submitting a Quota Increase Request Step 4: Open Request Modal and Test Input Validation Action: Select the All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests entry ➔ Click the orange Request increase at account level button. Modal Context: The dialog displays: Description: The maximum number of vCPUs for all running or requested Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instances per Region. Requested for: Account ID 887086382708. Region: United States (N. Virginia) us-east-1. Testing Input Validation: In the Increase quota value field, enter 32 (matching the current limit). Console Feedback: An immediate red client-side validation error is triggered: ❌ Must be a number greater than your current quota value of 32
Technical Takeaway: AWS enforces robust UI-level validation to prevent redundant, no-op support ticket submissions. Step 5: Input Target Limit of 64 vCPUs and Submit Input Parameter: Increase quota value: Enter 64 (doubling compute capacity to support parallel distributed workloads with Spot cost savings). AWS Approval Notice: ℹ️ Approvals: For some services, smaller increases are automatically approved, while larger requests are partially approved or routed to AWS Support for engineering review.
Action: Click Request to transmit the formal quota increase application. 🔹 Module 3: Tracking Approval Lifecycle and Verifying Resolution Step 6: Monitor Progress via the Service Quotas Dashboard Action: Return to the primary Service Quotas console ➔ Navigate to Dashboard or Quota request history. Review “Recent quota increase requests”: Service: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) Quota name: All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests Request type: User Requested quota value: 64 Status: Case Closed (Support ticket reviewed and successfully completed) Request date: 21 thg 10, 2026 Last updated date: 21 thg 10, 2026 Step 7: Receive Official Email Confirmation from AWS Support Delivery Channel: Primary administrator Gmail inbox linked to account trangiabao. Subject: Service Quota Increase Notification from AWS Support. Email Body Content: “Hello there,
Thank you for your patience while I was working on your request.
I am pleased to inform you that your quota increase has been approved. For your convenience, I have included details of the approved Quota here:
[US East (Northern Virginia)]: EC2 Spot Instances / All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests, New Limit = 64
The new quota will take effect in 30 minutes and you can see the newly approved quota on your Service Quotas console…”
Step 8: Inspect Resolution in AWS Support Center Action: Click the Help icon in the top header ➔ Select Support Center ➔ Navigate to Your support cases ➔ Select the closed ticket. Support Case Verification: Plan: Basic Support (Standard complimentary tier). Timestamp: Wed Oct 21 2026 15:49:28 GMT+0700. Technical Outcome: Support engineers confirmed that the New Limit = 64 configuration has been committed to the us-east-1 capacity allocator. Propagation Window: A propagation window of approximately 30 minutes is allocated for worldwide distributed control planes to complete consistency synchronization. 🔹 Module 4: Managing Service Quotas Programmatically via AWS CLI In addition to Console workflows, cloud infrastructure engineers automate service quota audits and limit requests using the AWS CLI v2.
Step 9: Query Service Codes for EC2 Discover canonical service identifiers:
aws service-quotas list-services \ --query "Services[?contains(ServiceCode, 'ec2')].{Code:ServiceCode, Name:ServiceName}" \ --output table Step 10: Query Current Spot vCPU Limit via Quota Code L-34B43A08 Inspect the active value in us-east-1:
aws service-quotas get-service-quota \ --service-code ec2 \ --quota-code L-34B43A08 \ --region us-east-1 \ --query "Quota.{QuotaName:QuotaName, QuotaCode:QuotaCode, Value:Value, Unit:Unit, Adjustable:Adjustable}" \ --output json Sample JSON Response: { "QuotaName": "All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests", "QuotaCode": "L-34B43A08", "Value": 64.0, "Unit": "None", "Adjustable": true } Analysis: The "Value": 64.0 field confirms system-wide convergence on the 64 vCPU limit, while "Adjustable": true confirms this is an elastic soft quota. Step 11: Scripting Automated Quota Increase Requests Submit a quota adjustment programmatically:
aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase \ --service-code ec2 \ --quota-code L-34B43A08 \ --desired-value 64 \ --region us-east-1 Step 12: Inspecting Quota Request History via CLI Audit the status of historical submissions:
aws service-quotas list-requested-service-quota-change-history-by-quota \ --service-code ec2 \ --quota-code L-34B43A08 \ --region us-east-1 \ --query "RequestedQuotas[*].{ID:Id, Status:Status, DesiredValue:DesiredValue, Created:Created}" \ --output table 🔹 Module 5: Proactive Limit Monitoring with CloudWatch Alarms To safeguard auto-scaling groups and distributed jobs against unexpected throttling exceptions, production architectures pair Service Quotas with CloudWatch Alarms:
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm \ --alarm-name "EC2-Spot-vCPU-Quota-Utilization-High" \ --alarm-description "Trigger alarm when Spot vCPU utilization exceeds 80% of the 64 vCPU ceiling" \ --namespace "AWS/Usage" \ --metric-name "ResourceCount" \ --dimensions Name=Service,Value=EC2 Name=Type,Value=Resource Name=Resource,Value=SpotInstances \ --statistic Maximum \ --period 300 \ --threshold 51.2 \ --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold \ --evaluation-periods 1 \ --alarm-actions arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:887086382708:aws-cli 💡 Troubleshooting & Real-World Lessons: 1. Cloud Economics Question: Does increasing a Service Quota from 32 to 64 vCPUs incur billing charges? Technical Reality: ABSOLUTELY NOT. AWS Billing Model: A Service Quota is purely a “safety ceiling” designed to prevent runaway costs caused by operational mistakes, runaway scripts, or security breaches. Submitting an increase request and having it approved to 64 vCPUs is 100% free of charge. AWS only bills for actual compute consumption—measuring seconds of active instance runtime. If your account holds a limit of 64 vCPUs but runs 0 active instances, your EC2 bill remains exactly $0.00. 2. Client-Side Input Validation (“Must be a number greater than your current quota value of 32”) Root Cause: Attempting to submit a request with the value 32, identical to the active baseline. Resolution: Submissions must specify a positive integer strictly higher than the current value (e.g., 64 or 128). Values must be backed by architectural requirements to avoid administrative review rejections. 3. Differentiating Soft Quotas vs. Hard Quotas Soft Quotas: Administrative safeguards that can be adjusted via Service Quotas or AWS Support tickets (e.g., EC2 vCPUs, Elastic IP allocations, DynamoDB provisioned capacity). Hard Quotas: Immutable architectural or protocol limits fixed by AWS service design (e.g., DynamoDB maximum item size of 400 KB, SQS payload maximum of 256 KB, maximum VPC peering connections per route table). 4. Regional Scope of Quotas (Per-Region Quotas) Observation: Increasing the Spot vCPU quota to 64 in us-east-1 (N. Virginia) leaves other regions (e.g., ap-southeast-1 Singapore) at their default 32 vCPU limit. Best Practice: In multi-region deployments or disaster recovery configurations, quota adjustments must be initiated and tracked independently for each designated target region. 5. Shift from Instance-Count Limits to vCPU-Based Quotas Historical Context: Historically, AWS throttled EC2 instances by gross instance count (e.g., 20 instances). This treated a lightweight t3.nano (2 vCPUs, 0.5 GB RAM) identically to a massive c5.18xlarge (72 vCPUs, 144 GB RAM). Modern Model: By measuring raw vCPU capacity, organizations enjoy granular elasticity to deploy diverse instance combinations up to their aggregate compute ceiling. 6. Propagation Delay (~30 Minutes) Behavior: Attempting to launch instances immediately following ticket closure might briefly yield MaxSpotInstanceCountExceeded errors. Mechanism: AWS operates a massive global control plane. A brief 15 to 30-minute consistency window is necessary for the new capacity quota to replicate to every placement engine across Availability Zones. 7. Account Justification for High-Volume Increases Risk Management: For new AWS accounts, AWS enforces conservative baseline limits to mitigate fraudulent activity, unauthorized cryptocurrency mining, or DDoS botnet creation. Operational Tip: When requesting high-magnitude quota jumps, provide clear use-case justifications in the description field (e.g., “Training deep learning models for university capstone research”). 8. Automated Multi-Account Quota Templates Enterprise Scaling: Organizations utilizing AWS Organizations can configure Quota Request Templates. When new member accounts are provisioned, approved quota increases are automatically requested across all member environments without manual administrative intervention. 📌 Summary & Skills Acquired: Through the Resource Limit Governance with AWS Service Quotas lab, the intern has acquired:
Thorough comprehension of resource quota governance on the AWS cloud platform. Complete practical execution of the vCPU quota increase lifecycle (L-34B43A08) from 32 to 64 vCPUs. Cohesive integration between the Service Quotas Console, AWS Support Center, and Email notification channels. Proficiency in programmatic quota querying and proactive threshold monitoring utilizing the AWS CLI and Amazon CloudWatch, establishing the foundation for large-scale distributed deployments in upcoming weeks.

title: Hybrid DNS with Route 53 Resolver
content:
The Hybrid DNS with Route 53 Resolver (Hybrid DNS Management with Amazon Route 53) hands-on lab was conducted on Monday (12/10/2026) during Week 5. This page provides an exhaustive step-by-step implementation guide complete with precise IP CIDR allocations, nslookup validation commands, troubleshooting resolutions, and all 11 verification screenshots. 🔗 Lab Reference Material: Set up Hybrid DNS with Route 53 Resolver
🎯 Lab Objectives: Master network topology design and Hybrid DNS resolution bridging on-premises enterprise networks with AWS cloud environments. Automate multi-VPC networking infrastructure deployment via AWS CloudFormation. Configure Security Groups permitting bidirectional DNS queries (UDP and TCP Port 53) across VPC boundaries. Deploy AWS Directory Service (AWS Managed Microsoft Active Directory) acting as the authoritative on-premises enterprise DNS controller. Configure Route 53 Resolver Outbound Endpoints and Resolver Rules to conditionally forward queries originating in AWS to on-premises DNS servers. Configure Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints to receive and resolve incoming queries from on-premises clients targeting AWS Private Hosted Zones. Validate end-to-end bidirectional DNS resolution using nslookup. 📊 Provisioned Resource Specifications: Resource Name / Identifier Configuration & Detailed Specs Environment / Region Notes EC2 Key Pair hybrid-dns-keypair RSA, .pem format us-east-1 Administrative access to RDGW client CloudFormation Stack Hybrid-DNS-Stack Provisions On-Prem VPC, Cloud VPC, Subnets, Route Tables, NAT GW us-east-1 Automates multi-VPC baseline environment Security Group Route53-Resolver-SG Inbound: TCP/UDP 53 (DNS), Outbound: All traffic Cloud & On-prem VPCs Secures DNS Resolver query paths Microsoft AD corp.example.com AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard Edition On-Prem VPC Authoritative on-premises DNS controller Outbound Endpoint r53-outbound-resolver 2 IP Endpoints across 2 Availability Zones Cloud VPC Subnets Forwards AWS queries to On-Prem Resolver Forwarding Rule forward-to-corp-ad Forwards corp.example.com to Active Directory IPs Cloud VPC Association Routes on-premises domain queries Inbound Endpoint r53-inbound-resolver 2 IP Endpoints across 2 Availability Zones Cloud VPC Subnets Accepts on-premises queries to AWS Test Client EC2 RDGW-Client-Tester Windows Server 2022 / Amazon Linux Test Environment Executes nslookup validation scripts 🚀 Step-by-Step Implementation & Screenshot Gallery: Step 1: Create Administrative EC2 Key Pair (hybrid-dns-keypair) Action / Navigation: Open the Amazon EC2 console in us-east-1 (N. Virginia) ➔ In the sidebar, select Network & Security ➔ Key Pairs ➔ Click Create key pair. Configuration Parameters: Name: hybrid-dns-keypair Key pair type: RSA Private key file format: .pem (for SSH or Windows Administrator password decryption) Next Action: Click Create key pair and securely store the downloaded .pem file. Step 2: Deploy Multi-VPC Topology via AWS CloudFormation Action / Navigation: Navigate to AWS CloudFormation ➔ Click Create stack (with new resources) ➔ Select Upload a template file. Configuration Parameters: Stack name: Hybrid-DNS-Stack Parameters: Select Key Pair hybrid-dns-keypair created in Step 1 Purpose: Automatically provisions two isolated VPCs (simulated Cloud VPC 10.0.0.0/16 and On-premises VPC 192.168.0.0/16), establishes VPC Peering, Internet Gateways, Subnets, and Route Tables. Step 3: Select Security Group for Route 53 Resolver Endpoints Action / Navigation: Navigate to EC2 Console ➔ Under Network & Security ➔ Select Security Groups. Selection: Locate the designated Security Group named Route53-Resolver-SG (created by CloudFormation for Resolver endpoints). Step 4: Configure Inbound Rules (Allow Port 53 UDP & TCP) Action / Navigation: Select the Inbound rules tab ➔ Click Edit inbound rules. Configuration Parameters: Rule 1: Type DNS (UDP), Port 53, Source: On-premises VPC CIDR (192.168.0.0/16) and Cloud VPC CIDR (10.0.0.0/16) Rule 2: Type DNS (TCP), Port 53, Source: On-premises VPC CIDR (192.168.0.0/16) and Cloud VPC CIDR (10.0.0.0/16) Next Action: Click Save rules. 💡 Difficulties Encountered & Troubleshooting at Step 4:
A frequent pitfall is opening only UDP 53 while omitting TCP 53. Standard lightweight queries use UDP, but DNS queries exceeding 512 bytes (such as DNSSEC or large responses) automatically fallback to TCP. Without TCP 53, queries will experience intermittent timeouts. Always configure both UDP and TCP rules.
Step 5: Verify Port 53 Security Group Inbound Permissions Action / Navigation: Review the finalized Inbound rules table. Observation: Both DNS (UDP) and DNS (TCP) rules on port 53 are verified active across internal VPC ranges. Step 6: Provision AWS Managed Microsoft Active Directory Action / Navigation: Navigate to AWS Directory Service ➔ Click Set up directory ➔ Select AWS Managed Microsoft AD. Configuration Parameters: Edition: Standard Edition Directory DNS name: corp.example.com Directory NetBIOS name: CORP VPC: Select On-premises VPC (192.168.0.0/16) Subnets: Select 2 Private Subnets across distinct Availability Zones Purpose: Simulates the authoritative corporate Domain Controller and internal DNS server. Step 7: Inspect Directory Status & Note Active Directory DNS IPs Action / Navigation: Allow 15-20 minutes for directory provisioning, then open directory details. Details Recorded: Status: Active DNS address 1: 192.168.1.xxx DNS address 2: 192.168.2.xxx Note: These two DNS IP addresses represent target endpoints for Route 53 Resolver forwarding rules. Step 8: Provision Route 53 Resolver Outbound Endpoint (r53-outbound-resolver) Action / Navigation: Navigate to Amazon Route 53 ➔ Under Resolver, click Outbound endpoints ➔ Click Create outbound endpoint. Configuration Parameters: Endpoint name: r53-outbound-resolver VPC: Select Cloud VPC (10.0.0.0/16) Security Group: Select Route53-Resolver-SG verified in Step 5 IP addresses: Choose at least 2 Availability Zones, assign 1 subnet per AZ, and choose Auto-allocate IP Next Action: Click Submit. Verify operational status transitions to Operational. 💡 Difficulties Encountered & Troubleshooting at Step 8:
Route 53 Resolver strictly mandates a minimum of two IP endpoints residing in separate Availability Zones for High Availability redundancy. Selecting only one AZ halts the wizard.
Step 9: Configure Resolver Forwarding Rule for corp.example.com Action / Navigation: In the sidebar, select Resolver ➔ Rules ➔ Click Create rule. Configuration Parameters: Rule name: forward-to-corp-ad Rule type: Forward Domain name: corp.example.com VPCs that use this rule: Associate Cloud VPC Outbound endpoint: Select r53-outbound-resolver Target IP addresses: Enter the 2 Microsoft AD DNS IP addresses recorded in Step 7 (Port 53) Next Action: Click Submit. Step 10: Provision Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoint (r53-inbound-resolver) Action / Navigation: In the sidebar, select Resolver ➔ Inbound endpoints ➔ Click Create inbound endpoint. Configuration Parameters: Endpoint name: r53-inbound-resolver VPC: Select Cloud VPC (10.0.0.0/16) Security Group: Select Route53-Resolver-SG IP addresses: Choose 2 Availability Zones and matching subnets Purpose: Exposes static private IP addresses within AWS for on-premises DNS conditional forwarders to query AWS Private Hosted Zones (e.g., aws.local). Step 11: Validate Bidirectional DNS Resolution via nslookup Action / Navigation: Connect to the test instance (RDGW or Linux test client) and execute bidirectional DNS lookups. Commands Executed: # 1. Query on-premises domain from AWS Cloud via Outbound Endpoint nslookup dc01.corp.example.com # 2. Query AWS private hosted zone from On-premises via Inbound Endpoint nslookup app.aws.local <Inbound-Endpoint-IP> Output: Both lookups return resolved internal IP addresses without NXDOMAIN errors or timeouts, confirming seamless bidirectional Hybrid DNS operation. 📝 Summary & Key Takeaways: Seamless Hybrid DNS Architecture: Route 53 Resolver delivers an enterprise-grade DNS bridge, completely replacing burdensome, self-managed BIND forwarder instances on EC2. Clear Inbound vs Outbound Demarcation: Inbound Endpoint: Ingests external on-premises DNS queries into AWS to resolve Private Hosted Zones. Outbound Endpoint: Forwards internal AWS queries out to on-premises DNS controllers via Resolver Rules. Migration Acceleration: Enables migrating cloud workloads to interact with legacy on-premises databases, SAP, and ERP systems using standard internal domain names without rewriting network configuration strings.

title: Amazon Lightsail Deployment
content:
The Amazon Lightsail Deployment hands-on lab was conducted on Monday (05/10/2026) during Week 4. This page provides a comprehensive step-by-step execution guide complete with precise parameter values, CLI commands, troubleshooting resolutions, and verification screenshots. 🔗 Lab Reference Material: Simplified Computing with Amazon Lightsail
🎯 Lab Objectives: Familiarize with the simplified management console and core capabilities of Amazon Lightsail. Provision and manage a standalone Managed Relational Database (MySQL) on Lightsail. Deploy two web applications: WordPress and Prestashop (E-Commerce) connecting to the shared database. Configure the underlying Linux/Ubuntu environment, assign Static IPs, and define firewall rules. Implement data backup procedures using Snapshots and scale up workloads by upgrading instance plans (Migration). 📊 Provisioned Resource Specifications: Resource Name / Identifier Configuration & Detailed Specs Address / Ports Notes Lightsail Database Workshop-DB-Instance MySQL 8.0, Standard Plan ($15/mo, 1GB RAM, 2 vCPUs) Port 3306, Master User: LightsailAdmin Master DB: dbWordPress WordPress Instance WordPress-1 Blueprint: WordPress (Bitnami), Linux/Ubuntu Static IP: Attached, Port 80, 443 Connected to Lightsail DB Prestashop Instance Prestashop-1 Blueprint: Prestashop, Linux/Ubuntu Static IP: Attached, Port 80, 443 E-Commerce Platform Instance Snapshot wordpress-backup-snapshot Full point-in-time snapshot before instance upgrade Size: ~20 GB, Status: Available Used for scale-up Migrated Instance WordPress-Migrated Created from Snapshot, higher hardware bundle Static IP: Re-attached Seamless service continuity 🚀 Step-by-Step Implementation & Screenshot Gallery: Step 1: Provision a Managed Relational Database (MySQL) Action / Navigation: Log into the Amazon Lightsail console ➔ Navigate to the Databases tab ➔ Click Create database. Configuration Parameters: Deployment Region: ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) Database Engine: MySQL (version 8.0) Master Username: LightsailAdmin Master Password: Generate strong automated password or specify custom secure password Initial Database Name: dbWordPress Database Plan: Standard Plan ($15/month, 1 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs, 40 GB SSD, 100 GB Data Transfer) Database Identifier: Workshop-DB-Instance Identification Tags: Key = dbname, Value = dbWordPress Next Action: Scroll down and click Create database. Monitor the status transition from Creating to Available. 💡 Difficulties Encountered & Troubleshooting at Step 1:
Initializing a Managed Database on Lightsail typically takes 5 to 10 minutes. Immediately save the Master User (LightsailAdmin), password, and Endpoint hostname shown on the screen. Forgetting these credentials requires resetting master credentials, adding delay to application setup.
Step 2: Deploy WordPress Application Instance (WordPress-1) Action / Navigation: Navigate to the Instances tab on Lightsail ➔ Click Create instance. Configuration Parameters: Instance Location: Singapore (Zone A) Platform: Linux/Unix Blueprint: Select WordPress (pre-packaged Bitnami stack) Instance Plan: $5/month bundle (1 GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 40 GB SSD, 2 TB Transfer) Instance Name: WordPress-1 Next Action: Click Create instance. The virtual server launches in 1 to 2 minutes. Step 3: Connect via SSH & Configure Ubuntu OS Environment Action / Navigation: On the WordPress-1 instance card, click the orange terminal icon (Connect using SSH) to launch a browser-based shell session. Commands Executed: # Update Linux system package repositories sudo apt-get update -y # Inspect WordPress source application directory ls -la /opt/bitnami/wordpress Purpose: Verify OS integrity, permissions, and prepare configuration parameters needed to integrate with the remote database. Step 4: Network Configuration, Static IP Assignment & Firewall Rules Action / Navigation: Open instance details for WordPress-1 ➔ Select the Networking tab. Configuration Parameters: Attach Static IP: Click Attach static IP ➔ Name it StaticIP-WordPress-1 ➔ Attach to WordPress-1 (ensures persistent public IP address across reboots). IPv4 Firewall Rules: HTTP: Port 80 (TCP), Source: Custom / Anywhere HTTPS: Port 443 (TCP), Source: Custom / Anywhere SSH: Port 22 (TCP) restricted or default Lightsail policy. Step 5: Configure Database Connection & Initial WordPress Setup Action / Navigation: Open a new browser tab, navigate to http://<Static-IP-WordPress-1>. The WordPress Welcome setup wizard appears. Configuration Parameters: Database Name: dbWordPress Username: LightsailAdmin Password: [Master password saved in Step 1] Database Host: [Workshop-DB-Instance Endpoint]:3306 Table Prefix: wp_ Next Action: Click Submit ➔ Click Run the installation. 💡 Difficulties Encountered & Troubleshooting at Step 5:
If an “Error establishing a database connection” appears, common causes include: (1) An incorrect Database Host string (must be the complete Lightsail DB Endpoint hostname, never localhost), (2) Case sensitivity mismatch on database name (dbWordPress), or (3) The Managed DB is still initializing. You can verify network reachability from SSH via mysql -h <endpoint> -u LightsailAdmin -p.
Step 6: Validate & Access WordPress Admin Dashboard Action / Navigation: Once installation finishes, browse to http://<Static-IP-WordPress-1>/wp-admin. Configuration Parameters: Site Title: Cloud Journey Blog Username: admin Password: [Admin password] Email: trangiabao@example.com Result: Successfully authenticate into the WordPress Admin Dashboard, confirming that blog posts and application settings are persisted to the external Lightsail DB. Step 7: Deploy Prestashop Instance & Configure Networking Action / Navigation: Return to Lightsail Console ➔ Instances tab ➔ Create a new instance using the Prestashop blueprint ➔ Name it Prestashop-1. Configuration Parameters: Platform: Linux/Unix Blueprint: Prestashop Instance Plan: $5/month or $10/month bundle Instance Name: Prestashop-1 Networking: Attach a dedicated Static IP StaticIP-Prestashop-1, ensure Firewall rules allow ports 80 (HTTP) and 443 (HTTPS). Step 8: Complete Prestashop E-Commerce Setup Wizard Action / Navigation: Open a new browser tab, navigate to http://<Static-IP-Prestashop-1> to launch the 6-step Prestashop Installation Assistant. Configuration Parameters: 1. Welcome page: Select English ➔ Click Next. 2. License agreements: Check “I agree to the above terms and conditions”. 3. System compatibility: Verify all server environment checks show green checkmarks. 4. Store information: Shop name Cloud Store Demo, Activity Technology, Country Vietnam. 5. Database configuration: Database server address: [Workshop-DB-Instance Endpoint] Database name: dbPrestashop Database login: LightsailAdmin Database password: [Master DB password] Next Action: Click Test your database connection now! to verify database privileges before completing setup. 💡 Difficulties Encountered & Troubleshooting at Step 8:
The Prestashop installer requires SQL permissions for CREATE DATABASE, ALTER, and INDEX. If reusing LightsailAdmin, ensure the target schema dbPrestashop is either pre-created or the user has permissions to create new databases.
Step 9: Access Prestashop Enterprise Admin Dashboard Action / Navigation: Connect via SSH to Prestashop-1, remove the temporary installation directory for security compliance, then access the Back Office URL. Commands Executed: # Remove installation directory per security guidelines sudo rm -rf /opt/bitnami/prestashop/install Result: Successfully log into the Prestashop Back Office / Dashboard, displaying catalog management, order metrics, and business intelligence panels. Step 10: Create Point-in-Time Instance Snapshot Action / Navigation: In the WordPress-1 instance dashboard, navigate to the Snapshots tab ➔ Click Create snapshot. Configuration Parameters: Target Instance: WordPress-1 Snapshot Name: wordpress-backup-snapshot Purpose: Capture the full disk state, operating system, web server configuration, and application code prior to executing hardware migration. 💡 Difficulties Encountered & Troubleshooting at Step 10:
Snapshot creation reads and copies all disk blocks (~20 GB). During this window, avoid heavy database writes or software upgrades on the instance to guarantee point-in-time filesystem consistency.
Step 11: Monitor Snapshot Creation Progress Action / Navigation: Stay on the Snapshots tab to track real-time progress. Observation: The status displays Snapshotting… alongside a progress bar indicating data synchronization to underlying storage. Step 12: Verify Snapshot Availability Status Action / Navigation: After 5 to 8 minutes, refresh the snapshot list. Observation: The snapshot wordpress-backup-snapshot transitions to Available status with timestamp and disk footprint recorded. Step 13: Scale Hardware by Restoring Snapshot into a Larger Instance (Migration) Action / Navigation: Beside wordpress-backup-snapshot, click the three-dot action menu ... ➔ Select Create new instance from snapshot. Configuration Parameters: Region: Singapore (ap-southeast-1) Upgraded Instance Plan: $10/month bundle (2 GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 60 GB SSD) or $20/month bundle (4 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs) New Instance Name: WordPress-Migrated Static IP Reassignment Procedure: Once WordPress-Migrated is running, return to the Networking tab. Select StaticIP-WordPress-1 ➔ Click Detach from old WordPress-1. Click Attach and bind directly to WordPress-Migrated. Result: External visitors immediately access the upgraded, higher-capacity server without DNS downtime or configuration alterations. 💡 Difficulties Encountered & Troubleshooting at Step 13:
The most frequent pitfall during instance migration is forgetting to re-attach the Static IP address. If skipped, the new instance receives a random dynamic public IP, breaking existing domain names and bookmarks. Always verify static IP attachment after creating instances from snapshots.
📝 Summary & Key Takeaways: Simplicity of Lightsail: Amazon Lightsail delivers a bundle-based, intuitive management experience with predictable monthly pricing, making it ideal for blogs, SMB applications, and rapid prototyping. Decoupled Architecture Best Practice: Decoupling the database layer into a standalone Managed Database isolates mission-critical data from compute instances, simplifying maintenance and horizontal scaling. Seamless Vertical Scaling with Snapshots: Point-in-time snapshots serve as an efficient disaster recovery mechanism and provide a safe bridge for upgrading compute resources when business traffic increases.

title: Deploying Relational Databases with Amazon RDS
content:
The Deploying Relational Databases with Amazon RDS lab was executed on Thursday (01/10/2026) as part of Week 3. This page provides comprehensive technical documentation for designing a highly available, multi-Availability Zone (Multi-AZ) two-tier network architecture, configuring chained security group firewalls, provisioning an Amazon RDS MySQL instance, connecting an Amazon EC2 Web Server, and executing data protection workflows via Manual DB Snapshots and Point-in-Time Restore. 🔗 Lab Reference Source: Get Started with Amazon RDS Workshop
🎯 Lab Objectives: Master the architecture, high availability mechanisms, and operational best practices of Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service). Design and implement an isolated Two-Tier Architecture: placing the Web Server tier in a Public Subnet and the Database tier in isolated Private Subnets to enforce defense-in-depth security principles. Create a DB Subnet Group spanning across at least two distinct Availability Zones (us-east-1a and us-east-1b) to satisfy Multi-AZ high-availability requirements. Configure granular network isolation via Security Groups: restricting the MySQL inbound port TCP 3306 exclusively to traffic originating from the Web Server’s Security Group (ec2-sg), prohibiting direct ingress from the public Internet. Provision an Amazon RDS database utilizing the MySQL Community Edition engine, configured on the db.m5.large instance class with automated synchronous Multi-AZ Deployment enabled. Deploy an Amazon EC2 web workstation (Amazon Linux 2023), install Apache HTTP Server and the PHP runtime, configure connection strings to the private RDS Endpoint, and validate end-to-end CRUD operations. Execute database snapshot protection through Manual DB Snapshots, analyze automated daily backup windows, and understand disaster recovery workflows (Point-in-Time Recovery - PITR). 📊 Provisioned Resource Specifications: Parameter / Resource Actual Value Technical Significance & Role Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) rds-vpc (vpc-0d0b88a31c814b1df) Isolated virtual network environment with CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16 Public Subnet rds-subnet-public1-us-east-1a Public-facing subnet associated with an Internet Gateway, auto-assigns Public IPs Private Subnet 1 rds-subnet-private1-us-east-1a Isolated private subnet in us-east-1a hosting the Primary DB instance Private Subnet 2 rds-subnet-private2-us-east-1b Isolated private subnet in us-east-1b hosting the Standby DB replica DB Subnet Group rds-subnet-group Multi-AZ subnet collection designated for RDS database failover Web Security Group ec2-sg (sg-0cec4d0fbfc6d4c41) Inbound: Port 80 (HTTP from 0.0.0.0/0) & Port 22 (SSH from My IP) RDS Security Group rds-sg (sg-0331b33d6bf62d714) Inbound: Port 3306 (MySQL) restricted strictly to ec2-sg RDS Instance Identifier db-instance MySQL Community 8.0, Instance Class: db.m5.large (2 vCPUs, 8 GiB RAM) Deployment Mode Multi-AZ Deployment Synchronous secondary replica in another AZ for automatic seamless failover Database Name fcaj Initial database created upon deployment Master Username admin Root administrative credential for database management RDS Endpoint db-instance.cgnkaue6ib4x.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com Private canonical DNS endpoint resolving to port 3306 Web Server Instance web-server t2.micro, Amazon Linux 2023, Apache httpd & PHP 🏛️ Architecture Overview: The deployment adheres strictly to the AWS Well-Architected Framework:
📋 Detailed Step-by-Step Implementation Guide: 🔹 Module 1: Architecture Design & Network Infrastructure Preparation Step 1: Provision the Multi-AZ VPC (rds-vpc) Action: Sign in to the AWS Management Console ➔ Navigate to VPC ➔ Click Create VPC. Configuration: Select VPC and more for automated network topology creation. Name tag: rds-vpc IPv4 CIDR block: 10.0.0.0/16 Number of Availability Zones (AZs): 2 (us-east-1a and us-east-1b) Number of public subnets: 2 Number of private subnets: 2 NAT gateways: None (to eliminate unnecessary operational cost during lab testing) VPC Endpoints: None Action: Click Create VPC and verify completion across all network routing components. Step 2: Enable Public IPv4 Addressing for the Public Subnet Action: Go to Subnets ➔ Select rds-subnet-public1-us-east-1a ➔ Select Actions ➔ Edit subnet settings. Configuration: Check Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address ➔ Click Save. Objective: Ensures any web tier EC2 instances launched in this subnet automatically receive routable public IP addresses for incoming user traffic. 🔹 Module 2: Configuring Security Group Firewalls & DB Subnet Group Step 3: Configure Web Server Security Group (ec2-sg) Action: Navigate to Security Groups ➔ Click Create security group. Settings: Security group name: ec2-sg VPC: Select rds-vpc Inbound rules: Rule 1: Type HTTP, Port 80, Source 0.0.0.0/0 (allows general public access). Rule 2: Type SSH, Port 22, Source My IP (secures administrative shell access). Step 4: Configure Database Security Group (rds-sg) Action: Click Create security group again. Settings: Security group name: rds-sg VPC: Select rds-vpc Inbound rules: Type MySQL/Aurora, Port 3306, Source select Custom ➔ Enter the Security Group ID of ec2-sg (sg-0cec4d0fbfc6d4c41). Security Significance: Known as Chained Security Groups, this pattern ensures that no unauthorized machine from the Internet or within the VPC can connect to port 3306 unless it explicitly carries the ec2-sg tag. Step 5: Create DB Subnet Group Action: Open the Amazon RDS console ➔ Click Subnet groups ➔ Click Create DB subnet group. Settings: Name: rds-subnet-group Description: Subnet group for RDS MySQL Multi-AZ VPC: Select rds-vpc Availability Zones: Select both us-east-1a and us-east-1b. Subnets: Select the two Private Subnets associated with the selected AZs (10.0.128.0/20 and 10.0.144.0/20). Action: Click Create. 🔹 Module 3: Provisioning & Configuring Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ Step 6: Launch the Amazon RDS Instance Action: In the Amazon RDS console, click Databases ➔ Click Create database. Detailed Configuration Parameters: Database creation method: Standard create Engine options: MySQL (Community Edition 8.0) Templates: Production (enables the Multi-AZ configuration) Deployment options: Multi-AZ DB instance (Creates primary instance and synchronous standby replica) DB instance identifier: db-instance Master username: admin Master password: Set strong credentials DB instance class: Standard classes db.m5.large (2 vCPUs, 8 GiB RAM) Storage: General Purpose SSD (gp2/gp3), Allocated storage 20 GiB Virtual Private Cloud (VPC): rds-vpc DB subnet group: rds-subnet-group Public access: No (Enforces private internal network isolation) VPC security group: Choose rds-sg (remove the default group) Initial database name: fcaj Action: Click Create database and allow 10 to 15 minutes for complete automated provisioning. Step 7: Inspect Operational Logs, Events, and Automated Maintenance Observations: In the Connectivity & security tab, record the canonical Endpoint and Port 3306. In the Logs & events tab, inspect provisioning audit trails, initial automated snapshots, and synchronous replica creation logs. In the Maintenance & backups tab, verify that automated backups are enabled with a 7-day retention period and examine the scheduled maintenance window. 🔹 Module 4: Deploying Web Server (EC2) & Establishing Database Connectivity Step 8: Launch the EC2 Web Instance Action: Navigate to EC2 ➔ Click Launch instances. Parameters: Name: web-server AMI: Amazon Linux 2023 AMI Instance type: t2.micro Network settings: VPC rds-vpc, Subnet rds-subnet-public1-us-east-1a, Auto-assign Public IP: Enable, Security group: ec2-sg. Step 9: Install the Web Stack and Test Database Connectivity Action: Establish SSH connection into the EC2 instance via terminal: # Update software packages sudo dnf update -y # Install Apache HTTP Server, MariaDB client, and PHP MySQL extensions sudo dnf install -y httpd php php-mysqli php-pdo mariadb105 # Start and enable the Apache service sudo systemctl start httpd sudo systemctl enable httpd Verify network line of sight from EC2 to RDS: # Test TCP handshake on port 3306 nc -zv db-instance.cgnkaue6ib4x.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com 3306 Deploy PHP database verification script (/var/www/html/dbtest.php): <?php $servername = "db-instance.cgnkaue6ib4x.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com"; $username = "admin"; $password = "YourMasterPassword123"; $dbname = "fcaj"; // Create connection $conn = new mysqli($servername, $username, $password, $dbname); // Check connection if ($conn->connect_error) { die("Database connection failed: " . $conn->connect_error); } echo "<h1>Amazon RDS Database Connection Successful!</h1>"; echo "<p>Connected securely to database: <strong>" . $dbname . "</strong> via internal endpoint.</p>"; $conn->close(); ?> Validation: Open a web browser and navigate to: http://<EC2-Public-IP>/dbtest.php. The success banner validates flawless end-to-end multi-tier connectivity. 🔹 Module 5: Operational Resilience & Data Protection (Snapshot Backup & Restore) Step 10: Create a Manual DB Snapshot Action: In the Amazon RDS console ➔ Select db-instance ➔ Click Actions ➔ Take snapshot. Parameters: Snapshot name: rds-manual-snapshot-fcaj Action: Click Take snapshot. Architectural Purpose: Manual snapshots are stored durably in internal Amazon S3 storage across multiple AZs and persist until explicitly deleted by administrators, even if the source DB instance is terminated. Step 11: Database Recovery Workflow (Restore from Snapshot) Standard AWS Recovery Lifecycle: To initiate a restore, select the snapshot rds-manual-snapshot-fcaj ➔ Click Actions ➔ Restore snapshot. AWS creates a brand-new DB Instance with a distinct DNS endpoint, ensuring the production database is not accidentally overwritten. Once data integrity verification is completed, web tier connection strings are updated to point to the new endpoint to complete the disaster recovery cutover. 💡 Troubleshooting & Real-World Lessons: 1. Connection Timed Out Between Web Server and RDS Root Cause: Inbound security group rules on rds-sg did not permit port 3306 from the ec2-sg security group ID, or the RDS instance was placed in subnets lacking local route connectivity to the public subnet. Troubleshooting: Use nc -zv <RDS-Endpoint> 3306 directly from the EC2 shell to confirm Transport Layer connectivity before inspecting application application code. 2. Subnet Group Availability Zone Constraint Error Root Cause: When configuring Multi-AZ deployment, Amazon RDS enforces that the DB Subnet Group must cover at least two distinct Availability Zones. Resolution: Ensure that when creating rds-subnet-group, at least two subnets in separate AZs (e.g., us-east-1a and us-east-1b) are included. 3. High Availability Failover vs. Read Scalability Multi-AZ: Designed for High Availability (HA). The standby replica is an exact synchronous copy that does not accept read or write traffic. In a failure event, automated DNS failover redirects traffic to the standby within 60–120 seconds. Read Replicas: Designed for Read Scalability. They utilize asynchronous replication and expose individual endpoints to offload heavy analytical read traffic from the primary instance. 4. Cost Optimization & Resource Teardown Best Practice: The db.m5.large Multi-AZ configuration incurs notable hourly operational expenses. Upon finishing lab testing, create a final snapshot if data preservation is needed, and terminate the instance to prevent unnecessary charges. 📌 Summary & Skills Acquired: Through the Deploying Relational Databases with Amazon RDS lab, the intern has acquired:
End-to-end mastery in architecting secure, isolated multi-tier database topologies in the AWS Cloud. Hands-on proficiency in chained security group configurations and DB Subnet Group provisioning. Complete command over high-availability Multi-AZ failover and disaster recovery snapshot procedures.

title: Week 1
content:
Week 1 Objectives: Familiarize with cloud computing fundamentals and foundational infrastructure services following the Explore AWS Services curriculum on The First Cloud Journey. Master initial cost governance principles using AWS Budgets and implement robust identity governance according to the principle of least privilege with AWS IAM. Hands-on architecting and provisioning of isolated cloud networks (Amazon VPC), compute instance management (Amazon EC2), and object storage hosting (Amazon S3). Dedicate Friday to synthesizing weekly technical knowledge, finalizing comprehensive Worklog documentation, and formulating initial concepts for the internship Capstone Project Proposal. Tasks to be Carried Out This Week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material Monday Cost Governance & Identity Security: - Establishing account governance & budget alerts with AWS Budgets (000007). - Identity management and access control with AWS IAM (000002). - Enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all administrative access paths. 09/14/2026 09/14/2026 000007 & 000002 Tuesday Core Networking Infrastructure (VPC Essentials): - Provisioning an isolated cloud network via Amazon VPC (000003) (Subnets, Route Tables, Internet Gateway). - Implementing structural segregation between Public Subnets (Internet-facing) and Private Subnets (DB/Backend). 09/15/2026 09/15/2026 Amazon VPC Workshop (000003) Wednesday Elastic Compute Services (EC2 Compute Basics): - Launching and configuring virtual servers with Amazon EC2 (000004). - Configuring Security Groups, Key Pairs, SSH terminal connectivity, and web server installation. 09/16/2026 09/16/2026 Amazon EC2 Workshop (000004) Thursday Object Storage & Static Website Hosting (S3 Storage): - Provisioning S3 Buckets, uploading objects, and managing Storage Classes with Amazon S3 (000057). - Enabling Static Website Hosting and configuring public-read Bucket Policies. 09/17/2026 09/17/2026 Amazon S3 Workshop (000057) Friday Week 1 Review, Worklog Completion & Project Work: - Knowledge Review: Consolidate foundational services mastered throughout the week (IAM, VPC, EC2, S3). - Worklog Completion: Finalize bilingual Week 1 documentation and execute clean resource teardowns. - Project Work: Analyze business constraints and technical requirements for the Capstone Project Proposal. 09/18/2026 09/18/2026 FCAJ Roadmap Daily In-Depth Learning Outcomes & Key Takeaways: 📌 Monday (09/14/2026) - Cost Governance (AWS Budgets) & Identity Security (AWS IAM) What did we learn today? Proactive Cloud FinOps via AWS Budgets: Mitigated “bill shock” risks by establishing automated financial guardrails before deploying cloud infrastructure. Configured a Monthly Cost Budget capped at $10.00. Configured two automated notification thresholds: Actual spend reaching 80% ($8.00) and Forecasted spend reaching 100% ($10.00), triggering instant alert emails to prevent budget overruns. Zero-Trust Identity Hardening via AWS IAM: Locked down the Root Account, strictly adhering to the principle of never utilizing root credentials for day-to-day engineering activities. Created a dedicated IAM User admin-dev for hands-on technical operations. Enforced role-based access through IAM User Groups rather than attaching direct user policies, associating the AdministratorAccess AWS Managed Policy according to the principle of least privilege. Enforced strict Password Policies: minimum 12 characters requiring uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Enforced Virtual Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) via Google Authenticator across both Root and IAM User accounts. Figure 1.1.1: IAM identity governance topology enforcing least privilege resource access control.
Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Budget Notification Email Not Delivering: Email address syntax typo during budget creation prevented delivery. Solution: Verified notification parameters within AWS Budgets, resubmitted the recipient address, and confirmed the SNS subscription confirmation link via Gmail. MFA Lockout Risk During Device Reset: Acknowledged the critical best practice of securely archiving the MFA backup seed key offline to mitigate permanent account lockout. 📌 Tuesday (09/15/2026) - Isolated Cloud Networking via Amazon VPC What did we learn today? Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Subnet Topologies: Defined Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) blocks, creating VPC fcaj-vpc with 10.0.0.0/16 (allocating 65,536 private IP addresses). Subdivided the network across two Availability Zones (us-east-1a and us-east-1b): Public Subnets: 10.0.1.0/24 (AZ-a) and 10.0.2.0/24 (AZ-b) allocated for edge workloads (ALB, Web Servers). Enabled Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address. Private Subnets: 10.0.10.0/24 (AZ-a) and 10.0.20.0/24 (AZ-b) reserved for databases and application tiers, completely isolated from direct internet access. Traffic Routing via Internet Gateway & Route Tables: Provisioned Internet Gateway fcaj-igw and attached it to VPC fcaj-vpc. Created Private-Route-Table containing solely local internal routing 10.0.0.0/16 local, ensuring total internet isolation for backend workloads. title: Architecture Overview & Network Topology
content:
1. VPC Endpoint Core Mechanics A VPC Endpoint is a managed virtual networking component that facilitates private communication between your AWS VPC and supported AWS services without exposing traffic to public IP addresses, Internet Gateways, or NAT devices.
Attribute Gateway Endpoint Interface Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) Supported Services Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB Most AWS services (S3, SSM, EC2, CloudWatch), SaaS endpoints Routing Mechanism Injects an AWS Prefix List (pl-xxxx) directly into VPC Route Tables Provisions Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) with private IP addresses Access Reach VPC-internal only (bound to Route Table) VPC-internal AND on-premises (via Site-to-Site VPN / Direct Connect) Pricing Free of charge Hourly rate per ENI + Data processing charges (per GB) 2. Network Topology & Hybrid Simulation The architecture consists of two isolated VPCs designed to emulate a realistic hybrid enterprise environment:
VPC Cloud (10.0.0.0/16):
Represents the primary AWS cloud production environment. Hosts the Test-Gateway-Endpoint EC2 instance located inside an isolated private subnet with no Internet Gateway attached. Configured with an S3 Gateway Endpoint to validate private object transfer. VPC On-Premises (192.168.0.0/16):
Simulates an on-premises enterprise data center. Deploys an EC2 instance running StrongSwan IPsec VPN configured to establish an automated Site-to-Site VPN tunnel with an AWS Transit Gateway (TGW). Hosts the Test-Interface-Endpoint EC2 instance used to test secure S3 access through the VPN tunnel. [!NOTE] For cost optimization during hands-on practice, this lab provisions a single StrongSwan VPN instance. In enterprise production environments, always deploy redundant VPN appliances across multiple Availability Zones or pair AWS Direct Connect with an automated IPsec backup tunnel for high availability and fault tolerance.
