Worklog Completion: Finalize bilingual Week 9 documentation and teardown lab resources. - Project Work: Develop an end-to-end migration and cutover plan for the internship Capstone Project. 11/13/2026 11/13/2026 FCAJ Roadmap Daily In-Depth Learning Outcomes & Key Takeaways: 📌 Monday (11/09/2026) - Server Migration (Part 1): 7Rs Strategies & VM Import/Export What did we learn today? Systematic Evaluation via the AWS 7Rs Framework: Evaluated the architectural rationale behind each migration path: Rehost (Lift-and-shift): Migrating existing virtual machine disks directly into EC2 without code modifications. Replatform (Lift-tinker-and-shift): Substituting self-managed components with managed equivalents (e.g., self-hosted MySQL to Amazon RDS). Refactor / Re-architect: Redesigning monolithic applications into cloud-native microservices or serverless architectures. Repurchase: Transitioning to commercial SaaS solutions. Retain: Keeping sensitive workloads on-premises due to compliance or legacy coupling. Retire: Decommissioning redundant applications identified during discovery. Relocate: Rapidly moving VMware infrastructure to VMware Cloud on AWS without hardware conversion. End-to-End Execution of VM Import/Export: Built a baseline Ubuntu Linux web server on a local hypervisor environment. Exported the virtual machine hard disk image into .vmdk format. Created an Amazon S3 staging bucket fcaj-migration-staging-887086382708 and uploaded the .vmdk image. Configured the vmimport IAM Role with a trust policy for vmie.amazonaws.com granting S3 get and EC2 write access. Executed image conversion via the AWS CLI: aws ec2 import-image \ --description "Ubuntu Web Server Migration" \ --disk-containers "Format=vmdk,UserBucket={S3Bucket=fcaj-migration-staging-887086382708,S3Key=ubuntu-server.vmdk}" aws ec2 describe-import-image-tasks --import-task-ids import-ami-0abc123def456 Launched an EC2 instance from the generated Custom AMI, validating that the web daemon, local files, and network configurations remained intact. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Missing Kernel Virtualization Drivers on Boot: The converted EC2 instance stalled during initialization due to missing Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) and NVMe storage drivers. Solution: Booted into the source VM prior to export, updated the Linux kernel to install official AWS Nitro driver packages, and successfully re-imported the VMDK. 📌 Tuesday (11/10/2026) - Server Migration (Part 2): Continuous Block Replication with AWS MGN What did we learn today? Architecture of AWS Application Migration Service (MGN): Mastered how AWS MGN provides non-disruptive, block-level background replication directly from live operating systems, decoupling replication throughput from OS filesystem locks. Step-by-Step Production Migration Workflow: Configured the Replication Settings Template: Selected dedicated staging subnets, cost-efficient replication storage volumes (gp3/sc1), and KMS customer-managed encryption keys. Installed the lightweight AWS Replication Agent on the running host: wget -O ./aws-replication-installer-init.py https://aws-application-migration-service-us-east-1.s3.amazonaws.com/latest/linux/aws-replication-installer-init.py python3 ./aws-replication-installer-init.py --region us-east-1 --aws-access-key-id <KEY> --aws-secret-access-key <SECRET> Monitored initial block synchronization until the agent entered steady-state Continuous Data Replication. Launched non-disruptive Test Instances inside a staging VPC to validate application boot sequences, network routes, and database connectivity. Conducted the final Cutover: Changed instance state to Ready for Cutover, stopped source server processes, and launched the final production instance, achieving a business cutover window under 3 minutes. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Firewall Block on Replication Port (TCP 1500): The source agent reported Failed to connect to replication server. Root cause: Outbound firewall policies on the local perimeter blocked outbound TCP port 1500 traffic. Solution: Opened outbound TCP 1500 to the regional AWS MGN replication endpoints, enabling real-time TLS data streaming. 📌 Wednesday (11/11/2026) - Database Migration & Continuous CDC with AWS DMS & SCT What did we learn today? Automated Schema Translation with AWS SCT: Utilized the AWS Schema Conversion Tool to analyze source database structures, automatically transforming DDL scripts, constraints, sequences, and indexes into Amazon RDS MySQL specifications. Core Components of AWS Database Migration Service: DMS Replication Instance: Deployed a dedicated dms.t3.medium replication instance to manage transactional memory buffers and apply schema transformations. Source & Target Endpoints: Configured secure credentials and verified database connectivity with end-to-end connection tests. DMS Migration Task: Configured a task combining initial Full Load with continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) utilizing MySQL binary logging (binlog). Zero-Downtime Cutover Mechanics: Monitored the initial full copy reaching 100% completion while continuous write mutations (inserts/updates/deletes) streamed real-time. Verified that replica lag remained under 1 second before promoting the Amazon RDS instance to production primary. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: CDC Failing to Capture Live Transactions: The DMS task threw an error stating Binary logging not enabled on source database. Solution: Updated the source MySQL my.cnf configuration with mandatory binary log directives (log-bin=mysql-bin, binlog_format=ROW, binlog_row_image=FULL) and restarted the service. 📌 Thursday (11/12/2026) - Enterprise Networking with AWS Transit Gateway & DataSync What did we learn today? Hub-and-Spoke Topology via AWS Transit Gateway: Solved the combinatorial complexity of full-mesh VPC Peering ($N(N-1)/2$ connection pairs) by establishing a central cloud router. Each VPC connects to Transit Gateway through a single elastic network attachment. Segmented Traffic Routing via Dedicated Route Tables: Created Prod-Route-Table within TGW routing production traffic exclusively to the Shared Services VPC and explicitly dropping routes to development networks. Created Dev-Route-Table restricting development network packets within their isolated perimeter. High-Throughput File Migration with AWS DataSync: Deployed a local DataSync agent reading directly from on-premises NFS/SMB shares. Achieved accelerated, encrypted parallel transfers into S3 buckets with automatic SHA256 integrity checksum validations. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Asymmetric Routing Packet Drops: Connected VPCs were unable to ping one another across the Transit Gateway. Root cause: While routes were declared within the TGW route tables, the VPC subnet route tables lacked a static route sending destination CIDRs to the tgw-xxxx target. Solution: Updated local subnet route tables on both VPCs to route target ranges to the Transit Gateway. 📌 Friday (11/13/2026) - Week 9 Review, Worklog Finalization & Migration Runbook Engineering What did we learn today? Enterprise Migration Lifecycle Synthesis: Seamlessly unified server rehosting (AWS MGN), zero-downtime relational data migration (AWS DMS), centralized hub-and-spoke networking (Transit Gateway), and bulk file synchronization (DataSync). Disciplined Decommissioning Protocol: Decommissioned DMS replication instances, removed cutover test nodes, detached VPC attachments, and deleted Transit Gateway resources to prevent idle hourly billing. Production Cutover Runbook for the Capstone Project: Authored an exhaustive minute-by-minute migration runbook detailing database schema extraction, continuous replication steps, rollback procedures, and DNS switchovers for the graduation project.

title: Week 10
content: Week 10 Objectives: Master the Event-Driven Architecture (EDA) paradigm and modern asynchronous distributed design patterns on AWS. Architect, manage, and harden production-grade API endpoints using Amazon API Gateway (RESTful APIs, HTTP APIs, custom Lambda Authorizers, traffic shaping with Throttling & Usage Plans). Implement service decoupling and load-leveling buffers using resilient queues via Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) (Workshop 000078), performing deep-dive architectural comparisons between Standard and FIFO queues while isolating malformed payloads via Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ). Establish pub/sub broadcasting and intelligent cross-domain event routing via Amazon SNS and Amazon EventBridge. Orchestrate resilient, distributed business state machines with automated error catching and retries using AWS Step Functions. Dedicate Friday to synthesizing technical competencies, finalizing bilingual Worklog documentation, and embedding asynchronous messaging pipelines into the Capstone Project Proposal. Tasks to be Carried Out This Week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material Monday Enterprise API Management & Hardening with API Gateway: - Comparing REST APIs vs HTTP APIs (features, latency profiles, unit economics). - Configuring resources, HTTP methods, CORS policies, and direct Lambda integrations. - Authoring custom Lambda Authorizers to validate JSON Web Tokens (JWT). - Implementing Usage Plans, API Keys, and Token Bucket rate limiting. 11/16/2026 11/16/2026 Cloud Journey - Modernize Tuesday System Decoupling & Asynchronous Queuing with Amazon SQS: - Evaluating high-throughput Standard Queues vs strictly ordered FIFO Queues. - Optimizing poll efficiency and reducing costs via Long Polling (ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds = 20s). - Tuning Visibility Timeout parameters to prevent concurrent duplicate message processing. - Establishing Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) with redrive policies for fault isolation. 11/17/2026 11/17/2026 Serverless Workshop (000078) Wednesday Pub/Sub Messaging & Event Orchestration with SNS & EventBridge: - Constructing the Fanout pattern: Subscribing multiple independent SQS queues to one SNS topic. - Deploying default and custom event buses within Amazon EventBridge. - Crafting declarative JSON event patterns to filter and route events based on payload attributes. 11/18/2026 11/18/2026 Cloud Journey - Modernize Thursday Distributed Workflow Orchestration with AWS Step Functions: - Visualizing state machines in Workflow Studio using Amazon States Language (ASL). - Combining Task, Choice (branching logic), Parallel, and Wait states. - Configuring automated fault resilience with exponential backoff retries and catch blocks. 11/19/2026 11/19/2026 Cloud Journey - Modernize Friday Week 10 Review, Worklog Completion & Project Work: - Knowledge Review: Consolidate API Gateway, SQS queues, SNS topics, EventBridge, and Step Functions. - Worklog Completion: Finalize bilingual Week 10 documentation and teardown lab resources. - Project Work: Integrate asynchronous SQS buffering and Step Functions orchestration into the Capstone Proposal. 11/20/2026 11/20/2026 FCAJ Roadmap Daily In-Depth Learning Outcomes & Key Takeaways: 📌 Monday (11/16/2026) - Enterprise API Hardening via Amazon API Gateway What did we learn today? Architectural Trade-Offs: REST API vs HTTP API: HTTP API: Optimized for sub-millisecond overhead (up to 60% latency reduction), streamlined configuration, and over 70% cost savings compared to REST APIs, with native OIDC/OAuth2 authorization support. REST API: Feature-complete enterprise gateway supporting Usage Plans, API Keys, request/response data mapping templates, AWS WAF integration, and private VPC interface endpoints. Token Authentication with Lambda Custom Authorizers: Developed a serverless authorizer inspecting incoming Authorization: Bearer <JWT> headers. The function validates cryptographic signatures, generating an IAM policy document (Effect: Allow) granting resource execution only upon successful token validation. Traffic Shaping & Throttling Guards: Implemented the token bucket algorithm enforcing a steady-state rate limit of 100 requests/sec with a burst buffer of 200 requests. When requests exceed limits, the gateway returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, safeguarding downstream database connections. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Browser CORS Restrictions: Frontend single-page applications were blocked by browser cross-origin security. Root cause: Missing OPTIONS pre-flight handlers and CORS headers. Solution: Enabled CORS on the API Gateway console, ensuring standard headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*', Access-Control-Allow-Headers: 'Content-Type,Authorization') were injected into all response schemas. 📌 Tuesday (11/17/2026) - Decoupling & Reliable Queuing with Amazon SQS What did we learn today? Comparing Core Message Queue Modalities: Standard Queue: Provides virtually limitless transactional throughput and at-least-once delivery semantics, suitable for decoupled workloads tolerant of occasional out-of-order execution. FIFO Queue: Strictly enforces first-in, first-out ordering and exactly-once processing using MessageDeduplicationId hashes and logical serialization via MessageGroupId. FinOps Optimization with Long Polling: Replaced Short Polling with Long Polling (ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds = 20), keeping connections open until messages arrive, eliminating millions of empty empty-receive API calls and slashing SQS billable requests by over 80%. Visibility Timeout Management: Tuned VisibilityTimeout = 30s. When Worker A leases a message, it is hidden from other concurrent workers. If Worker A succeeds, it issues delete_message. If the worker crashes, the message reappears after 30 seconds for Worker B, ensuring zero message loss. Fault Isolation with Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ): Attached orders-dlq to the main queue with maxReceiveCount = 3. Malformed payloads causing processing exceptions are automatically moved to the DLQ after 3 failed attempts, keeping the main processing line unblocked. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: Duplicate Processing from Premature Visibility Expiry: Heavy worker tasks taking 45 seconds caused SQS to assume worker failure at the 30-second mark, redelivering the message to a second worker and generating duplicate database writes. Solution: Implemented heartbeat calls inside the worker logic invoking change_message_visibility to extend the processing lease dynamically. 📌 Wednesday (11/18/2026) - Event Distribution with Amazon SNS & EventBridge What did we learn today? The Fanout Distribution Topology: Created an Amazon SNS Topic order-created-topic with three independent SQS queue subscribers (billing-queue, inventory-queue, and shipping-queue). A single published order event fans out concurrently, allowing all three domains to process payloads in parallel without knowing about each other. Enterprise Event Bus via Amazon EventBridge: Explored the structural advantages of EventBridge for content-based message filtering directly on incoming JSON payload keys. Declarative Filtering Rules: Authored an Event Pattern rule to route high-value transactions ($1,000+) directly into an accelerated audit workflow: { "source": ["ecommerce.orders"], "detail-type": ["OrderCreated"], "detail": { "amount": [{ "numeric": [">=", 1000] }] } } Encountered Challenges & Solutions: SQS Subscribers Not Receiving SNS Messages: Subscriptions were active but subscriber queues remained empty. Root cause: SQS queue Access Policies lacked explicit permissions allowing the SNS Topic ARN to perform sqs:SendMessage. Solution: Updated the SQS resource-based access policy to authorize the SNS topic principal. 📌 Thursday (11/19/2026) - Visual Workflow Orchestration with AWS Step Functions What did we learn today? Declarative State Machines via Workflow Studio: Decoupled business orchestration logic from application runtimes, modeling workflows using the Amazon States Language (ASL). State Flow Coordination: Task State: Invokes AWS Lambda functions or publishes messages to Amazon SQS. Choice State: Evaluates branching logic based on runtime JSON values (e.g., verifying customer account balances). Parallel State: Concurrently executes independent sub-workflows (e.g., triggering billing and dispatching email notifications simultaneously). Resilience & Fault Recovery: Integrated automated Retry blocks configured with exponential backoff (BackoffRate = 2.0), coupled with Catch handlers to initiate compensating transaction rollbacks when encountering unrecoverable errors. Encountered Challenges & Solutions: State Input/Output JSON Path Mismatches: State executions failed because previous Lambda responses returned deeply nested structures, causing subsequent Choice states to evaluate empty paths. Solution: Standardized state contracts using JSONPath filters: InputPath, ResultPath, and OutputPath to shape payloads cleanly across state transitions. 📌 Friday (11/20/2026) - Week 10 Review, Worklog Finalization & Capstone Architecture Integration What did we learn today? Serverless Architectural Synthesis: Connected the end-to-end event-driven chain: client ingestion (API Gateway) ➔ load leveling (SQS) ➔ event fanout (SNS/EventBridge) ➔ resilient business orchestration (Step Functions). Clean Teardown Practices: Terminated temporary Step Functions state machines, deleted experimental SQS queues, and detached test API Gateway endpoints to avoid ongoing account charges. Graduation Capstone Integration: Architected asynchronous order ingestion and transaction processing state machines for the Capstone Project, eliminating synchronous inter-service blocking and single points of failure.
